invariants_checked: misc/pr-assets is marked export-ignore in .gitattributes as defense-in-depth alongside removal of upstream PR screenshot PNGs (misc/pr-assets/adopter-card-layout.png and misc/pr-assets/adopter-navigation.png remain absent from git ls-files).
test-reports and test-reports/** remain export-ignore so audit evidence JSON files never leak into customer git archive source bundles; all upstream notice byte-preservation attributes remain intact.
Workflow retains least-privilege top-level permissions (contents: read), 40-char commit SHA action pins, and ubuntu-24.04 runner configuration.
Zero GitHub Actions ${{ ... }} template expressions are interpolated inside run: shell blocks; runtime variables expand safely via shell environment variables.

Start DocReader gRPC server provisions an ephemeral 256-bit GRPC_AUTH_TOKEN (masked in logs and exported to GITHUB_ENV for Go client loopback authentication), stores the server PID under RUNNER_TEMP instead of /tmp, and fails fast with kill -0 if the process exits prematurely.

findings.summary: Start DocReader gRPC server launched python -m docreader.main without GRPC_AUTH_TOKEN, causing immediate fail-closed AuthConfigError (sys.exit(1)) under GENYEE's hardened AuthInterceptor and hanging 30s before failing CI; run: blocks also interpolated ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }} directly and wrote the server PID to world-writable /tmp/docreader.pid.

invariants_checked: Crate source download verifies 64-hex SHA-256 digests against licenses/sources/anydoc.tsv (stripping GNU sha256sum leading backslash escapes), removes pre-existing destination symlinks before curl -o, and deletes unverified tarballs immediately on checksum mismatch.

Unpacked crate trees are scanned with find -type l to reject symlinks before copying into third_party/anydoc-go/patched-anydoc, and archive installation verifies a regular non-symlink artifact and unlinks $dest/$lib_name prior to copy.

strip_llvm_lto_sections matches dotted/hyphenated LLVM bitcode section names (\.llvm[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+, including .llvm.lto) and stages objcopy output via a temporary file so cross-target objcopy failures never corrupt $dest/$lib_name in place.

findings.summary: prepare_patched_anydoc did not unlink pre-existing tarball symlinks before curl -o, left mismatched tarballs on disk on SHA-256 failure, and accepted symlinks inside unpacked crate archives; strip_llvm_lto_sections missed dotted .llvm.lto section names and mutated $dest/$lib_name in-place rather than staging via a temporary file.

invariants_checked: MarkdownImageUtil scans prose in guaranteed O(N) linear time while preserving fenced code blocks (_transform_outside_fences) and paired inline backtick code spans (_inline_code_spans), preventing O(N^3) ReDoS on unclosed ![...](data:image/...) or ![...](...) inputs and preventing unclosed inline-code image openers from hiding subsequent real images.

extract_base64 enforces pre-decode base64 character caps (derived from MAX_INLINE_IMAGE_BYTES = 20 MiB) before slicing/decoding, per-document count (1000) and cumulative byte (100 MiB) budgets, strict raster MIME subtype allowlisting (blocking SVG/XML/EMF/WMF/EPS and path-traversal subtypes), and Pillow header verification under Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 40_000_000 with DecompressionBombWarning promoted to error.
MarkdownParser performs zero outbound network fetches on external http/https image URLs, delegating remote image downloads exclusively to Go's SSRF-guarded ImageResolver.ResolveRemoteImages.

findings.summary: MarkdownImageUtil regexes (b64_pattern, image_pattern, replace_pattern) suffered O(N^3) catastrophic backtracking on unclosed ![alt](data:image/...) and ![alt](...) inputs (>8s at n=400 / 12.8 KB), and an unclosed '![' inside an inline code span caused b64_pattern to span across prose and skip extracting a subsequent real base64 image.

MarkdownImageUtil.extract_base64 lacked pre-decode base64 payload size caps and per-document budgets (allowing oversized inline base64 OOM), omitted Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 40_000_000 raster header validation (allowing multi-hundred-megapixel PNG decompression bombs to bypass Go's ResolveDataURIImages checks via result.ImageRefs), and interpolated raw data:image/<subtype> strings into image_path (allowing ../ traversal, SVG/vector MIME types, and spoofed non-raster payloads).

invariants_checked: All upstream inline-code and fenced-code base64 preservation tests plus 4 new GENYEE security regression tests pass deterministically without writing bytecode caches or host paths.

MCP Rerank model guidance accurately documents that external MCP services and built-in MCP Server search_knowledge/grep_chunks endpoints do not require Rerank, while smart-reasoning Agents using built-in search_knowledge do.
All internal links and all 3 Mermaid diagrams in 08-mcp.md parse with 0 errors and 0 legacy upstream brand residues.

Core ER Mermaid diagram and internal links pass validation with 0 errors and 0 legacy upstream brand residues.

AdopterShowcase sanitizes adopterIssue and adopter.link.href via sanitizeExternalHttpUrl, omits empty links, attaches target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" to all external anchors, and loads scenario icons strictly from local ${homeAssets}/adopters/ SVGs.
adopters.module.css uses --gy-* design tokens exclusively (defined in shared/brand.css) with zero legacy CSS custom property prefixes.
siteNavigation links to '/#adopters' under GENYEE '行业场景' framing and keeps repositoryUrl empty.
sanitizeExternalHttpUrl enforces http:/https: protocols only, rejects ASCII control characters, and rejects URLs carrying embedded username/password userinfo.

findings.summary: sanitizeExternalHttpUrl permitted http:/https: URLs containing embedded username/password userinfo (e.g. https://user:secret@example.com or @-authority phishing URLs https://genyee.com@evil.example) to pass through into external anchor href attributes.
findings.regression_test: UP-DOCS-WEB-001: sanitizeExternalHttpUrl rejects embedded userinfo credentials and dangerous schemes
